program.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Make her close her jacket fully

outcomes.description: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
outcomes.target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.
outcomes.reference: The woman's jacket in the input image.

nodes.question: Does comparison of the same woman's jacket front closure in the source and edited images establish progress toward closing it?
nodes.criteria: Pass if identifiable corresponding front edges or closure segments show that the jacket has been brought together more than in the source. Fail if an adequately inspectable comparison establishes that the closure is unchanged or more open, with no evidenced closing progress. Unknown if either relevant closure is insufficiently visible, correspondence is uncertain, or the change cannot be established. A change in pose, silhouette, or drape alone establishes neither progress nor lack of progress.
nodes.binding: Identify the red jacket worn by the woman in both images. Compare its actual front closure, allowing for the change from a mostly frontal source view to a turned edited view. Describe observable closure edges or segments supporting the comparison. Do not equate a projecting panel with an open closure unless its relation to the front edges is visible.

nodes.question: Does direct inspection of the edited jacket establish that its front closure is fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible evidence establishes that the front panels meet along the entire intended closure with no remaining opening. Fail if at least one actual remaining opening along that closure is visibly established. Unknown if folds, draped fabric, pose, resolution, or occlusion prevent establishing either full closure or an actual opening. Failure to see the closure is not evidence of an opening.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited image directly for the same woman's red jacket. Use s1 only for garment identity and comparison context, not as proof of the endpoint. Identify the intended front edges and any observable closure line or genuine gap. Distinguish an opening between those edges from a loose panel, overlap, fold, or obscured surface.

nodes.question: Does the edited jacket's projecting or hanging panel provide identifiable evidence of an actual opening between its front closure edges, rather than merely a fold, overlap, or obscured view?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the panel can be traced to a front closure edge and visible separation from the opposing closure edge establishes a remaining opening. Fail if the relevant panel geometry is sufficiently visible to establish that this apparent gap is instead a fold, overlap, or other non-opening feature. Unknown if the front-edge relationship cannot be identified or is obscured. Fail only rejects this particular apparent-gap inference; it does not establish full closure.
nodes.binding: Investigate the projecting red panel in the edited image using s1's garment identification and s2's endpoint observations as ancestor context. Independently inspect the relationship between the panel, the opposing front edge, and any exposed intervening region. Do not simply repeat an ancestor's open/closed conclusion, and do not infer closure from the absence of a discernible gap.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s2, and s3_panel_attachment. Full closure is positively established by s2 pass. Incompleteness is positively established by s2 fail or s3_panel_attachment pass. If both full closure and incompleteness are positively established, return unknown because the observations conflict. Otherwise return complete when s2 passes, even if s1 or s3_panel_attachment is unknown. When incompleteness is established without conflicting full-closure evidence, return partial if s1 passes, absent if s1 fails, and unknown if s1 is unknown. If neither full closure nor incompleteness is established, return unknown. A diagnostic fail only rejects the particular panel-as-gap interpretation; it supplies neither completion nor progress. Supporting checks earn no completion credit independently, unrelated changes count as no requested progress, and unresolved evidence must not be converted into failure.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

s1: The binding is malformed and underspecified: replace the “(...)” placeholder with a stable subject reference, and make the node explicitly assess the requested *fully closed* end state as well as any visible progress. The traces repeatedly return unknown because the edited pose turns away and the draped panel hides the closure; they do not establish either completion or absence of progress. In the images, the source is more frontal and the edited view is turned sideways, with a large panel projecting away from the body. That silhouette alone cannot show whether the front edges meet. Keep the distinction between visible closure evidence and pose/drape, and allow unknown when the relevant edges cannot be compared; do not force the reference “yes” or infer closure from the panel. Improve the evidence request to inspect any visible closure/edge cues in both views and state what is actually observable, while preserving the criterion that full completion requires the jacket to be fully closed. The repeated high-confidence unknowns are a robustness/evidence limitation, not a transport or dependency failure (all checks are valid, queried, and dependency-free).

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment composition is incomplete: it returns unknown for several evidence combinations that establish a clear outcome. In particular, if s2 passes (full closure is positively established) but s3_front_gap is unknown because a segment is obscured, completion is still established by s2; the rule instead returns unknown. Likewise, if s2 fails and s3_front_gap passes (a remaining opening is established), s1 being unknown does not make the endpoint unknown: the jacket is incomplete, so the result is partial only if progress is evidenced, otherwise no if no progress is evidenced, and unresolved only when progress evidence is unresolved. The current exact combinations omit these cases and do not faithfully compose known endpoint and progress evidence.
